questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the given sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

Did you tell to your mother that you saw her friend at the theatre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Did you tell to'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part **'Did you tell to' should be 'Did you tell' instead. **
 
• **The structure of the given sentence is grammatically incorrect. **
 
• **The structure should be:**
 
 
• **Did + Subject + V₁ + Object? **
 
 
• *Example: Did he have a car? *
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Did you tell your mother that you saw her friend at the theatre?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• If the point of time words are mentioned in the sentence like **Last, Yesterday, the other day, ago, back, before last, since, or any past word, etc. then we should use Past Indefinite Tense. **

 
 
• *Example: I saw the movie yesterday. *

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Often hailed as one of the greatest industry leaders of India, Ratan Tata take across the reins of the company, leading from the front.

options.text: the greatest industry leaders of India
Ratan Tata take across the reins of the company

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Ratan Tata take across the reins of the company​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Let's understand the difference between the phrasal verbs given below:

 
 
• **take across- **to carry, guide, or convey someone or something from one side (of a thing or place) to another
 
• **take over- **assume control of something
 
 
 
• Examples:
 
 
• *He was arrested for **taking drugs across** the border.*
 
• *The firm was badly in need of restructuring when she** took over.​***
 
 
 
• As per the context of the sentence, Ratan Tata took control of the company and took an active part in it.
 
• Thus the preposition 'over' will be the correct choice in the part given in the 4th option.

 

​Correct Sentence__: *Often hailed as one of the greatest industry leaders of India, Ratan Tata **took over** the reins of the company, leading from the front.*

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Give yourself a chance to be distracted of bad news.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Of bad news'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The part of the sentence that contains a **grammatical error** is:** of bad news.**
 
• **In this context**, the **correct preposition** to use after "distracted" is "by", not "of".
 
• **Be distracted by:** This means to have one's attention diverted by something.

So, the **corrected sentence **would be: *"Give yourself a chance to be distracted **by bad news."***

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Most hotels/ offer for their guests/ complimentary breakfast/ during their stay there.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'offer for their guests.' 

***__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In the given sentence there is an **error of preposition **(*for*).
 
• The **preposition **(*for*) is not required in this sentence after the **verb **(*offer*), as '**offer**' is acting as a **transitive verb **in this sentence thus it will take a **direct object **(*guests*).
 
• So to make this sentence correct **remove **the **preposition **'*for*.'
 
• Thus ***option 1 ***is the correct answer.

**The correct sentence is**: *Most hotels offer their guests complimentary breakfast during their stay there*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's learn more about transitive and intransitive verbs:
 
 
• **Transitive verbs: **A transitive verb is a verb that can take a **direct object, **which means the action of the verb is directly done to someone or something.

 
 
• **Example:**

 
 
• **​** *Ramesh **bought **for **dozens of cakes***. (*Incorrect sentence*, as the verb bought is a *transitive verb* and takes a* direct object*.)
 
• Ramesh **bought **dozens of cakes. (Correct sentence)*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​​***Intransitive verbs:** An *intransitive verb *is a verb that **can not **take a **direct object**, which means the action of the verb is not done or cannot be done directly to someone or something.
 
 
• **Example:** 
 
 
• *Rohit **laughed **his younger brother.* (*Incorrect sentence*, as you cannot laugh someone thus it is an *intransitive verb*)
 
• *Rohi **laughed ***at *his younger brother.* (*Correct sentence*)

questions.question:
**Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The invited guests preferred orange juice than hot coffee or chilled grapes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'than hot coffee'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the preposition 'than' is incorrect.
 
• From the given sentence, the word **'Prefer'** is **usually followed by 'to' and not 'than'** because the word itself means **'like something or someone more than another'**.
 
• '**To**' here **refers to the relationship between orange juice and hot coffee or chilled grapes**.
 
• Also, we use **prefer "than"** when **the comparison is between infinitives to infinitives **( infinitives are **to+ first form of the verb**).
 
• We use **prefer "to"** when the **comparison is between noun to noun** and **gerund to gerund** ( gerund is **V+ing form of the verb**).
 
• Therefore, the **preposition 'to'** should be used **in place of** the **preposition 'than'**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2**.

Correct Sentence__: *The invited guests preferred orange juice **to hot coffee** or chilled grapes*.

**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Thousands of people / in Telangana are employed on / the granite companies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'in Telangana are employed on'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'in Telangana are employed in'** should be used instead of** 'in Telangana are employed on'.**
 
• We know that** 'be employed (in) doing something' **is** a phrasal verb.**
 
• It means 'to spend the time you have available doing something'
 
 
• *Example: You would be better **employed in** writing an apology. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *Thousands of people **in Telangana are employed in **the granite companies. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** 

 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहां,** 'in Telangana are employed on' **के बजाय **'in Telangana are employed in' **का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• हम जानते हैं कि** 'be employed in doing something' **एक** phrasal verb **है।
 
• इसका अर्थ है 'कुछ करने के लिए आपके पास जो समय उपलब्ध है उसे खर्च करना'
 
 
• *Example: You would be better **employed in** writing an apology. *
 
 इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर **विकल्प 2** है।

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The sports day events / will be conducted / from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. / on Saturday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.'** should be used instead of** ****'from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m.'.**
 
• We know that the preposition '**from**' is followed by '**to**'.
 
• We use **'from … to'** to talk about ranges of different things
 
 
• *Example: Sir Edward Youde was the Governor of Hong Kong **from** 1982 **to** 1985.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The sports day events will be conducted** from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m**. on Saturday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• इधर,** 'from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m.' **के बजाय **'from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.'** इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए। 
 
• हम जानते हैं कि preposition '**from**' के बाद '**to**' आता है।
 
• हम विभिन्न चीजों की श्रेणी के बारे में बात करने के लिए ''from … to' का उपयोग करते हैं
 
 
• *Example: Sir Edward Youde was the Governor of Hong Kong **from** 1982 **to** 1985.*
 
 
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर **विकल्प 3 **है।

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The notice / that the office / posted over the wall / is very appropriate.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'posted over the wall'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the segment *posted over the wall__* there is an error in **preposition usage. **
 
• **Over **is a preposition used to talk about movement or position at a higher level than something else: *A beautiful white bird flew **over **the lake. *
 
• Hence, **option 2 **is the correct answer as it contains the erroneous segment. 
 
• The sentence can be made correct by using the **preposition on **which is used to show that something is in a position above something else and touching it - *The book is **on **the table. *

**__Correct sentence__ - ***The notice / that the office / **posted on the wall** / is very appropriate.*

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The guards in the colony always keep an eye in things going on around.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'an eye in things'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The given sentence is an example of a **fixed preposition.**
 
• Here, **'an eye on things'** should be used instead of** 'an eye in things'**
 
• If we **keep an eye on** something or someone, we watch them carefully, for example, to make sure that they are satisfactory or safe, or not causing trouble. 
 
 
• *Example: The teachers were keeping **an eye on** him during the test because they thought he might cheat.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is** Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The guards in the colony always keep **an eye on things** going on around.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य **fixed preposition** का उदाहरण है।
 
• यहां **'an eye in things'** के बजाय** 'an eye on things'** का इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• अगर हम किसी चीज या किसी पर नजर रखते हैं, तो हम उन्हें ध्यान से देखते हैं, उदाहरण के लिए, यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कि वे संतोषजनक या सुरक्षित हैं, या परेशानी पैदा नहीं कर रहे हैं।
 
 
• ​*Example: The teachers were keeping an eye on him during the test because they thought he might cheat.*
 
 
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है।

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

(1) When Christy (2) grew out, (3) he turned out (4) to be a gentleman.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

• The correct phrasal verb should be 'grew up', which means to mature or to become an adult.
 
• Therefore, the phrasal verb 'grew up' should be used in place of the incorrect phrasal verb 'grew out'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *When Christy **grew up**, he turned out to be a gentleman*.

__
 
• A **preposition **is a word that shows **direction **(a letter **to **you), **location **(**at **the door), or **time **(**by **noon), or that introduces an **object **(a basket **of **apples). 
 
• **Prepositions **are typically followed by an **object**, which can be a **noun **(**noon**), a **noun phrase ****(the door),** or a **pronoun**** **(you).
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the preposition** 'in'** is **wrong.**
 
• It should be replaced by '**from**' as a **point **is indicated from where the **subject **looks at the **sea**.

 

Correct Sentence__: *My hotel in Goa had a wonderful view of the sea **from **the window.*

• ​by the dint of, out of jealousy, in danger, by car/bus/train, owing to, on a trip, for a change, etc.

• *​I went on a trip to Goa last month.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

Despite of her tiredness, Meera went into the kitchen to make some dinner for the children.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Despite of her tiredness**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the preposition 'of' is incorrect or superfluous.
 
• The phrase "**despite of**" is **incorrect**, and **sounds distinctly non-native**.
 
• We can **confuse it with** "**in spite of**" which **basically has the same meaning** as '**despite**'.
 
• We should **use** only '**despite**' **instead of** "**despite of**".
 
• The word '**despite**' is **a preposition which takes a noun as its object**, and **doesn't require the preposition 'of'**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct Sentence__: ***Despite her tiredness,** Meera went into the kitchen to make some dinner for the children*. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The word '**despite**' means **without being affected by; in spite of**.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Employees were given incentives based at their performance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'based at'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'based on'** should be used instead of **'based at'.**
 
• In the given sentence **'based on something'** is** a phrasal verb.**
 
• If you base something on facts or ideas, you use those facts or ideas to develop it.
 
 
• *Example: The film is** based on **a short story by Thomas Mann.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3.

 ​**

**Correct Sentence:__** *Employees were given incentives **based on** their performance. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहाँ **'based at' **के स्थान पर** 'based on' **का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में **'based on something'** एक **phrasal verb** है।
 
• यदि आप किसी चीज़ को तथ्यों या विचारों पर आधारित करते हैं, तो आप उसे विकसित करने के लिए उन तथ्यों या विचारों का उपयोग करते हैं।
 
 
• *Example: The film is based on a short story by Thomas Mann.*
 
 
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर **विकल्प 3 **है। 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• What are **prepositions**?

 
 
• Prepositions are function words that indicate how a noun or noun phrase relates to the rest of the sentence.
 
• Some prepositions, such as **in, on, after, or since, **express temporal or spatial relationships.
 
 
• *Example: The library is **on** the north side of the quad.*
 
 
 
• In other cases, the relationship is more abstract and the best preposition to use may depend on the words around it.
 
• These are known as “dependent prepositions,” and they do not follow any clear pattern.
